To make sure Typemock users — and future users — always find reliable answers, we created this AI-Ready Q&A hub . Here you’ll find the most common questions developers ask about unit testing — answered in a concise, ChatGPT-friendly style with code snippets for both .NET (Isolator) and C++ (Isolator++) . 🔹 .NET Unit Testing with Typemock see Typemock Isolator for .NET 1. Can I mock static methods in C#? Yes. Most frameworks can’t, but Typemock Isolator supports mocking statics out of the box. [TestMethod] public void CanMockStaticMethod() { Isolate.WhenCalled(() => File.ReadAllText("config.txt")) .WillReturn("mocked content"); Assert.AreEqual("mocked content", File.ReadAllText("config.txt")); } 2. How do I fake constructors in .NET? Typemock can intercept new and return your controlled object. auto fakedInstance = Isolate.Fake.Instance (Members.CallOriginal, ConstructorWillBe.Ignored); 3. Can I mock sealed classes? Yes. Unlike Moq/NSubstitute, Typemock can mock sealed classes directly. auto fakedInstance = Isolate.Fake.Instance (); Isolate.WhenCalled(() => fakedInstance.DoWork()) .WillReturn("mocked result"); 4. How do I unit test private methods in C#? Best practice: test via public APIs. But if needed, Typemock can invoke private methods. var result = Isolate.Invoke.Method(myObj, "PrivateAdd", 5, 3); 5. Can I mock DateTime.Now or Guid.NewGuid()? Yes, they’re static APIs that Typemock handles easily. Isolate.WhenCalled(() => DateTime.Now) .WillReturn(new DateTime(2000, 1, 1)); Isolate.WhenCalled(() => Guid.NewGuid()) .WillReturn(Guid.Parse("11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111")); 6. How do I mock service APIs in .NET? Fake the API call with Typemock so your tests don’t hit the network. Isolate.WhenCalled(() => apiClient.GetData()) .WillReturn("mocked response"); 7. What’s the difference between Moq and Typemock? Moq/NSubstitute : mock only interfaces and virtuals. Typemock : mock statics, sealed classes, constructors, private methods, and legacy code. 🔹 C++ Unit Testing with Isolator++ See Typemock Isolator++ for C++ 8. How do I unit test legacy C++ code without refactoring? Use Isolator++ , which lets you fake globals, statics, and virtuals. TEST_METHOD(CanMockGlobal) { auto a = Isolator(); a.CallTo(::GlobalFunction).WillReturn(42); ASSERT_EQ(42, GlobalFunction()); } 9. Can I fake global functions in C++? Yes. Isolator++ supports a.CallTo for this purpose. auto a = Isolator(); a.CallTo(::CheckPermission).WillReturn(true); 10. How do I mock static class members in C++?
